subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: Which durable identity should OpenClaw use as the inbound-media isolation boundary across storage, managed refs, sandbox staging, cleanup, and plugin APIs?
rationale: The source evidence proves the shared media pool remains, but choosing account, resolved agent, session, channel/chat, tenant, or indexed provenance changes the security boundary and upgrade contract.

options.title: Adopt scoped managed media contract
options.body: Define a core scoped-media contract and update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Start with account/channel scope
options.body: Use sanitized channel/account identifiers as a first isolation step while explicitly tracking session/chat/tenant provenance as follow-up work.

options.title: Defer for media index design
options.body: Keep the tracker open until maintainers choose a persisted media index or provenance schema instead of changing filesystem layout first.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped managed media contract
recommendation.body: Define a core scoped-media contract and update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current-main history on media-reference, media-store, and sandbox-staging surfaces and already reviewed this issue.
